note: The React port's own hooks. Only VALUES change; the KEYS are the contract probe.mjs addresses the app through - and clients[].id is one of them (it becomes the report key client.perClient.<id>). Filled through SURFACE 1 (landing + app header), SURFACE 2 (nav capsule, client hero, name flight) and SURFACE 4 (FAB, arc, narrator chip, chat lifecycle - dummy hook names throughout, only fabWrap moved to #fabwrap). Later-surface entries still carry the dummy's value and fail until minted - that is the gate working, not a broken map. THE BOOK IS THE APP'S BOOK: the port serves the injected C360 bundle, so the three client SLOTS point at the port's real accounts; slot 3 has no Meridian and takes the book's distressed relationship. heroName/ringTargetAttrPx/ringEndOffsetPx differ from baseline by design; nameMatchesExpected and ringHitsExpectedTarget gate the real contract. SURFACE 5 (workroom + odometer): the room MOUNTS rather than toggling a class, so `workroom` resolves to `.wk-root` while it is open and to `body` once it is gone, and `workroomShowClass` is the root's own class, so `roomClosed` therefore reads false-on-body without the probe having to null-check. The odometer hooks are the foundation's (`.eg-odo` / `.eg-odo-strip` / `eg-odo-blur`), the halo's keyframe is `wk-aurarot`, and the wash keyframe is `ancwash` on the hero's committed anchor (`#ancExposure` / `#ancExpV`, both new in this surface). `workroomExecute` is the mode's own primary label rather than the dummy's 'Execute write': the flow card's control says what the plan actually does, and it is the LAST control in the card so the probe's positional fallback still finds it. 0.9.29 (backlog row 59) moved that control into the room's GLASS register (`.wk-approve.wk-sheet-go`, no longer `.eg-btn-ink`) and dropped 'Approve and' from its wording, because it files a staged plan and is not a credit approval; `.wk-approve` is unchanged and is what every drive selects on. UNIFY-ROUTER (founder, 2026-08-31): Modification and Renewal collapsed into ONE 'Facility Actions' satellite, so the arc carries FOUR and `arcModify` now resolves to #actFacility - the key is the probe's contract and only the value moved. The room it opens is unbound and asks which route this is; the workroom flow's typed line binds `modify` implicitly and the ritual behind the question is unchanged. THE SALESFORCE BUBBLE (founder, 2026-09-01): the arc's fourth seat is `#actSalesforce`, which routes NOWHERE - it fans a second tier of two smaller glass bubbles (`.sfbtn`, `#sfAccount` / `#sfPackage`) that open the client's Account record and their Product Package in the org, in a new tab. The tier's open state is the `tier` class on #fabwrap, alongside `open`. `arcButton` deliberately stays `.arcbtn` so the arc's geometry leaves measure the FOUR satellites and never the branch; a tier bubble with no resolvable host or package id renders as a `.sfbtn.is-dead` span rather than an anchor. This restores the four-satellite, 30deg, r=96 geometry this file already documents - the three-satellite interlude between 668b840 and 86f0c35 was never minted here.
